articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Logistic Regression and Random Forest Algorithm for Cyber Attacks Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research aims to compare the performance of Logistic Regression and Random Forest algorithms in classifying cyber-attack types. Using a data set consisting of 494,021 data points with 42 attributes, an evaluation was conducted to assess the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of both algorithms. The results of the analysis show that Random Forest is superior to Logistic Regression in classifying cyber-attack types, with the accuracy of the Random Forest algorithm on 80:20 and 70:30 ratios resulting in a value of 99% compared to the accuracy of Logistic Regression on 80:20 ratio resulting in a value of 91% and on 70:30 ratio data can produce an accuracy value of 81%. This research provides a deeper insight into the ability of both algorithms to overcome the challenges of classifying cyber-attack types, which can be valuable for the development of a more effective cyber-attack detection system.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Motorized Valve System Based on DC Motor Integrating Rotary Encoder Sensors and Full State Feedback Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the performance of a DC motor-based motorized valve system that integrates a rotary encoder sensor and a full-state feedback controller. A DC motor is used as a drive to replace the conventional valve lever. The integration of the rotary encoder sensor allows precise measurement of the valve position, while the full-state feedback controller is used to regulate the system response by considering the entire state of the system. The modeling process is carried out using a transfer function in the z domain to obtain the full state feedback gain that matches the desired specification, which is 0% overshoot. This research involves mathematical modeling of the system, prototype testing, and system performance analysis based on the valve position response to the control signal. The results of this analysis are expected to provide insight into the effectiveness of using DC motors, rotary encoder sensors, and full-state feedback controllers in improving the performance of an authorized valve system. It is hoped that this research can serve as a foundation for further development in the use of efficient and accurate motorized valve systems.

articleTitle: Univer Metric to Measure the Degree of Universal Verifiability in E-Voting
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Election officials can use the Universal Verifiability verification model to compare the election results with the actual ballots that were used. Univer Metrics have been developed in this study to gauge the e-voting system's level of Universal Verifiability. The degree of Universal Verifiability in three voting protocols—Cortier, the Modified Threballot, and the Traditional Voting Protocol in Indonesia—is measured by the e-voting protocol that includes Universal verification. For the Modified Threballot Protocol, this implementation yields the highest Universal verifiability score of 1, meaning that the intended level of universal verifiability has been attained.

articleTitle: Advanced Malware Analysis Methods: Behaviour-Based Detection and Reverse Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The tesla malware agent attacked around 4.1% of the networks of various industrial companies. Agent tesla malware can harvest user credentials from various popular applications including Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and Google Chrome, becoming a global threat in various sectors and organizations around the world. In addition, the problem is that hackers using the agent tesla malware adopt more sophisticated spear-phishing campaigns and can use more sophisticated social engineering techniques to exploit vulnerabilities. So, with these problems, deeper analysis and implementation of holistic security measures are needed to combat threats, knowing the characteristics and ways to overcome the agent tesla malware in maintaining system and data integrity. This research focuses on overcoming this problem by comparing methods using behavior-based detection (virtual machine), behavior-based detection (sandbox), and reverse engineering to analyze the agent tesla malware. Behavior-based detection is used to observe malware activity when it is running on a computer or virtual machine. Meanwhile, reverse engineering is used to obtain the source code of the malware. The results of the agent tesla malware research analysis obtained using this method are that the malware can steal information from the victim's computer such as the computer username, as well as email and password information contained in the browser. The way the agent tesla malware works is to infect the system, read data on the computer and save the necessary data. Based on the test results in this research, the behavior-based detection (sandbox) method can reveal more actions in the malware with a total of 3877 or 185% more than the reverse engineering method.

articleTitle: Study of UAV Mobility Pattern on 5G Downlink Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: UAV as aerial base stations are increasingly popular for enhancing network coverage and capacity, particularly when rapid and flexible deployment is necessary. It can offer widespread connectivity from above due to their inherent flexibility and high mobility. This study investigates the effects of different UAV mobility patterns on the performance of 5G downlink transmission, with an emphasis on Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) and Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA) downlink transmission. The research investigates four different UAV movement patterns: circle, lemniscate, trifolium, and quadrifolium. Using simulation models, UAV trajectories are generated for each mobility pattern, and the resulting data rates are computed for both NOMA and OMA schemes. The results indicate significant variations in data rates across different mobility patterns and access schemes. Specifically, the trifolium curve pattern demonstrated the highest average. The lemniscate curve and quadrifolium pattern showed moderate performance better than circle. The circle pattern, while covering a broader area, resulted in lower average data rates.

articleTitle: Comparison of Cellular Network Coverage Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Conventional Models
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for predicting signal range in wireless communication networks, offering significant improvements over conventional models. Traditional methods, such as empirical path loss models, rely on predetermined formulas and parameters that may not fully capture the complex variability of real-world environments. In contrast, machine learning algorithms leverage large datasets to learn intricate patterns and dependencies within the data, resulting in more accurate and robust predictions. Moreover, machine learning demonstrates better adaptability compared to traditional methods because it does not depend on fixed formulas, allowing it to adjust more effectively to diverse and changing conditions, especially in complex urban environments where signal propagation is affected by numerous variables. This advancement not only improves network planning and optimization but also ensures higher service quality for end-users. Therefore, incorporating machine learning into signal coverage prediction marks substantial progress in creating more efficient and dependable wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Data Processing and Visualization in Software Defined Vehicular Network Tested
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The invention of the internet has revolutionized various fields, promoting rapid progress across many sectors, including economics, social sciences, politics, geography, and entertainment. Advancements in computer networks and transportation have mutually reinforced each other. A notable development is Software-Defined Networking (SDN), which uses a dynamic and centralized approach by separating control and data planes. Concurrently, the transportation sector is evolving with automation and advanced sensors in vehicles, supported by simulation software like Mininet for SDN networks and SUMO for road traffic. Despite their importance in developing Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), Mininet and SUMO are not integrated for simulating Software-Defined Vehicular Networks (SDVN) and are command-line-based, making them less user-friendly. To address this, we developed a web application that integrates Mininet and SUMO, providing user-friendly simulations for SDVN. This tool allows users to input parameters such as topology, vehicle count, protocols, speed, and transmission power, and outputs processed and visualized simulation data. Our SDVN testbed aims to support researchers in automated vehicles and ITS, advancing SDN applications in transportation. This integration facilitates realistic and comprehensive simulations, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation. With our project, we also do some visualization for the simulation. By making these tools accessible, we hope to accelerate advancements in SDN and ITS, ultimately benefiting society by paving the way for more connected and efficient intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Wideband Microstrip Antenna Design Using LoRa and GPS for Collision Warning Application
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This paper provided a design for a microstrip antenna with a wide bandwidth covering the LoRa and GPS working frequencies. The antenna is designed for vehicle-to-vehicle communication needs, enabling data sharing of location information as a form of collision warning. The designed microstrip antenna operated at frequencies of 915 MHz and 1575 MHz by trimming most of the ground plane to achieve bandwidth widening, followed by fine-tuning to achieve optimal results. The final design of the microstrip antenna, measuring 60 mm x 75.1 mm, exhibited a return loss of around −20 dB both at 915 MHz and 1575 MHz. The obtained VSWR values are around 1.22 both at 915 MHz and 1575 MHz. The proposed and fabricated antena has wideband characteristic and has operational frequency range from 822 MHz to 1820 MHz.

articleTitle: Development of Monitoring System for Early Childhood Education Learning Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: ECE (Early Childhood Education) is important for children learning since it sets a benchmark of learning for children when they begin schooling. However, identification of child development in the context of ECE has been found to be a huge challenge. The objective of this study is to design a highly effective monitoring system based on deep learning, object detection, and YOLO to improve the correctness and speed of monitoring ECE learning progress. Through the use of this technology, the system is designed to be able to analyses and categorise different activities of children in realtime with the feedback to the teachers and parents being immediate. It makes the process of monitoring much easier apart from enhancing communication between the teachers and the parents, not forgetting the progressive growth of the children. This capability was tested based on data captured by cameras placed in the classrooms then passed through yav8 to improve its accuracy as well as real-time monitoring abilities. The study shows how technology application in monitoring ECE improves the system's ability to meet the need of the children.

articleTitle: Implementation of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for Prediction of Tourist Arrivals in Pamoyanan Hill
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Pamoyanan Hill is a popular hill tourist destination in Subang Regency and suitable for visitors of all ages. Unexpected fluctuations in the number of visitors can affect the income and development of this tourist attraction. This study aims to develop a prediction model for the number of tourist visits to Pamoyanan Hill using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method of the backpropagation algorithm. Implementation is carried out by dividing the data into training and testing data. The evaluation showed an average accuracy rate of 90.04% and an average error of 9.96%. The use of scenarios with a proportion of 80% training data and 20% testing provides optimal results. The ANN parameters used include: number of input neurons 2, number of hidden layers 10, number of outputs 1, alpha 0.01, and iterations of 1000. The activation function used is binary sigmoid. The parameters are set to achieve the best results, with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.02347103. Keywords

articleTitle: Development of Data Compression Techniques for IoT Data Transmission in Isolated Aquaculture Using LoRa Through LoRaWAN Gateway Antares Telkom
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Aquaculture in remote areas challenges significant monitoring due to limited internet access. This research develops and implements an IoT communication system using LoRa RFM95W module, ESP32 microcontroller, and Telkom's LoRaWAN Gateway Antares for efficient and reliable sensor data transmission. LoRa operates in the 920–923 MHz band which offers long-range communication with low power consumption and is ideal for remote IoT applications. Class A LoRaWANare selected for power efficiency and an optimal Spreading Factor (SF) is chosen to balance coverage, data rate and power consumption. Data compression techniques are applied to minimize data loss, reduce data size, optimize bandwidth usage and ensure real-time data integration. Experiments with various compression algorithms and distances showed that the unishox2 algorithm achieved the best compression ratio, capable of transmitting data sizes of up to 347 bytes with minimal signal loss on SF9.

articleTitle: Multi-Step-Ahead Prediction of User Movement on 5G Networks Using the Long Short-Term Memory Method
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Since the initial launch of 5G networks in 2018, 5G technology has rapidly expanded to cover about 40% of the world's population, offering higher bandwidth, faster connectivity, and lower latency than 4G. However, due to its higher frequency operation, 5G necessitates more frequent handovers, making efficient handover performance crucial. This research focuses on enhancing handover efficiency by predicting user movement using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for multi-step-ahead prediction. The model created will utilize 60 seconds of historical data to predict 10 seconds ahead, with a target to achieve an average prediction accuracy of less than 20 meters with a latency under 100 ms. The study employs TensorFlow for model training, leveraging the Grab-Posisi dataset, and utilizes Plotly and TensorBoard for result visualization. Six model variations were trained, with the 16-unit model trained for 3106 epochs performing best, achieving 16.99 meters accuracy and 31 ms latency. The findings suggest that LSTM is effective for predicting user movement in 5G networks, with potential accuracy improvements through extended training epochs.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Weight-Based Goods Sorting System Using Robot Arm 5 DOF
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Large companies today compete in terms of innovation to enhance overall productivity by leveraging their technology with high speed, accuracy, reliability, and ease of operation as tools to support their productivity. Another challenge faced in the industry is the continuous weighing and sorting of objects. Regarding labour and time-related issues, one solution that can be employed is a manipulator robot. Therefore, this system provides an integrated approach to issues in the delivery, logistics, and packaging industries. Based on this background, this research is conducted to design a sorting application system for a 5 - degree of freedom (DOF) robot arm with 1 gripper, equipped with a load cell as a weight sensor, and controlled by Arduino. The developed system will function to sort objects based on weight categories. The weight sensor can provide accurate and precise measurements, which are crucial in ensuring the robot works precisely according to the commands. With this information, the robot can adjust its movements according to the carrying load and prevent overloading. This research aims to produce a robot arm capable of moving loads of 10 grams, 15 grams, 20 grams, 25 grams, and 30 grams in specified directions and angles, following a predefined program on Arduino.

articleTitle: Line Detection and Classification of Macroscopic Wood Images Using Hough Line Transform and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Wood is a natural material derived from trees or other plants, characterized by a hard, tough fibrous structure. Identifying wood species is crucial in the wood industry to ensure species conformity and to meet quality and legality standards. To prevent identification errors that can result in economic losses and environmental damage, a fast and accurate wood identification tool is essential. The aim of this research is to develop an automated system for measuring the density distribution of lines and obtain the line features in macroscopic wood images. One method that has been used involves the Hough Line Transform for detecting and extracting lines, combined with Random Forest algorithm for classification. This research focuses on three wood species that have distinct line patterns in their appearance. A confusion matrix was used to represent the performance of the model, with 70% of the data used for training and 30% for testing. All three wood species showed a very high accuracy when using this classification model. Lengkeng had the lowest accuracy at 93%, while Meranti and Puspa had the highest accuracy at 97%. The evaluation showed that the model accurately classified the line density in the macroscopic wood image, yielding final classes such as very close, close, wide, and very wide.

articleTitle: Implementing Microservice Architecture for An Elevator Monitoring System to Improve Scalability and Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The demand for more efficient and reliable elevator monitoring systems has increased due to security and safety issues in high-mobility buildings. This paper proposes a microservice architecture for an elevator monitoring system to enhance scalability, flexibility, and fault tolerance by decomposing the system into more minor, loosely coupled services. This paper will discuss the proposed system's design, implementation, and evaluation. The system, equipped with ESP32Cam and ultrasonic sensors, excels in real-time monitoring. Data is processed and analyzed using Python and OpenCV, allowing the system to not only count the number of people in the elevator but also detect any anomalies, ensuring the safety of the occupants. LED notification alerts, managed by NodeMCU8266, are triggered based on ultrasonic sensor data. MongoDB handles user management and analytical data, while the dashboard offers a user-friendly interface for real-time monitoring and system management provide essential information for elevator operators. The architecture's use of MQTT ensures efficient communication between sensors and services, creating a robust, scalable, and efficient solution.

articleTitle: Frontend Subsystem Development In Traditional Market Digitalization E-Commerce Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Traditional market e-commerce applications aim to expand the market reach and potential buyers of traders in traditional markets, develop low-cost and sustainable solutions, and facilitate the dissemination of real-time data information about products and buyers' desires that are easy to see, and able to communicate directly. between traders and buyers. The Virtual Market application is designed to fulfill general activities that occur in traditional markets, such as buying and selling activities, conversations and advertising. The main characteristic of shopping in traditional markets is that there is bargaining between traders and buyers, so this application presents a bargaining feature that will facilitate this activity. This application will go through a testing and verification stage to determine that the application created is in accordance with the specified final assignment objectives. In this paper, the frontend system will be designed and designed as a whole, starting from designing the application by considering the user interface and user experience to implementing the design on mobile devices using the chosen programming language.

articleTitle: Evaluation of User Experience E-Learning Website of Sangga Buana University Using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) Method
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The development of information technology is rapidly changing the interaction and behavior of society as well as the tasks of individuals and organizations, including in the education sector, which has led to the transformation of learning methods, such as e-learning systems. Sangga Buana University implements an e-learning system through a website platform as the main means for the student learning process. As something new, the Online Lecture website certainly has room for improvement. This research aims to evaluate the user experience of the Sangga Buana University Online Lecture platform using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) method. UEQ is a comprehensive measurement tool for assessing User Experience (UX) with six rating scales: attractiveness, clarity, efficiency, accuracy, stimulation, and novelty. Through sampling with a simple random sampling method, this study involved 110 respondents. The results showed a positive evaluation of the user experience of the Online Lecture website. All scales assessed in the UEQ show encouraging values. Aspects such as attractiveness, clarity, and efficiency scored in the “Good” category, while accuracy, stimulation, and novelty scored “Above Average”. The Online Lecture Website can further improve the accuracy, stimulation, and novelty scales.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Rectangular Patch Antenna Array for Uplink and Downlink in The Starlink Low Earth Orbit Satellite Communications System
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research investigates the development of a rectangular microstrip antenna array, employing an aperture coupled patch feeding technique, specifically designed to facilitate communication between ground stations and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, operating across the X-band and Ku-band frequencies (10.7-12.7 GHz for downlink and 14-14.5 GHz for uplink). Microstrip antennas, characterized by thin metallic patches on a dielectric substrate, known for their compact size and ease of integration, aim to improve coverage and signal quality from Starlink satellites. Simulations in CST Studio Suite optimized key parameters, resulting in a return loss below -10 dB and VSWR below 2, indicating effective impedance matching. The antenna demonstrated gains of 15.33 dBi for downlink and 12 dBi for uplink, with a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 6.3 to 7.7 degrees. Fabrication results confirmed a downlink gain of 15.2 dBi and an uplink gain of 12 dBi, with an HPBW of 5°. The design maintains acceptable side-lobe levels from -8.7 dB to -12.8 dB. The prototype meets expected specifications and future research on antenna arrays, high-power amplifiers (HPA), and low-noise amplifiers (LNA) could expand internet access in underserved regions of Indonesia, considering both social and economic factors.

articleTitle: IoT-based Environmental Monitoring System using Thermohygrometer MHB 382-SD and ESP 8266
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Bandung Metrology Directorate is one of the calibration laboratories that must provide guaranteed measurement results for calibrated measuring instruments. ISO 17025 requires monitoring, control, and recording of environmental conditions according to standards. Currently, laboratory environmental monitoring is still manual, requiring additional data processing to ensure that temperature and humidity are appropriate. Therefore, an IoT system was designed to monitor environmental conditions in real-time. The data collection method involves comparing data sent from RS 232 to the dashboard, taking into account the timing. Periodic and on-change data comparison methods, variations in the providers used, and the sequence of data transmission were also conducted. The results show that the information data sent from RS 232 to the Arduino IoT Cloud dashboard can be transmitted accurately. Furthermore, data sent periodically every 1 second compared to onchange data has an average difference of 0.06 seconds. Data sent periodically is more consistent than on-change data sent only when there is a change in data. The provider also greatly affects the speed of data transmission and reception. The sequence of received data is unstable and inconsistent, but this is not significantly apparent in the dashboard due to the very fast average data transmission of 0.19 seconds. Unstable internet signals or connections, IoT device failures, errors in data processing on the server or web application side can result in inconsistent data arrangement

articleTitle: Fashion Classification and Recommendation System Based on User Body Shape Using Convolutional Neural Network and Content Based Filtering Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Consumers currently have unlimited access to a variety of online products and services, including clothing. Despite significant progress, online clothing shopping often has challenges, especially in choosing clothing designs that match the user's body shape type, especially for women to support their appearance. Choosing the right clothes can increase the wearer's confidence and comfort. Therefore, it is necessary to create a tool that can be used by the public in choosing the right clothes. This study aims to design and implement a clothing classification and recommendation system that combines artificial intelligence and content-based recommendation techniques. The CNN method is used to classify the user's body shape type based on the images taken and then the system will provide clothing recommendations that match the user's body shape type using the Content-Based Filtering method. This system can integrate CNN methods very well to classify the user's body shape type and then recommend products that match the classified body shape type using the CBF method. Dataset scenario with 90% training data, 10% testing data and learning rate of 0.001 produces very good accuracy with training results of 96.61% and testing results of 85.71%. This system can provide a more satisfying shopping experience, providing assurance that each clothing choice is not only fashionable but also in line with the user's visual identity and preferences.

articleTitle: Design of A Smart Gateway Based on REST API for Data Transmission System Between Edge Devices and Server in The Aquaculture Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The focus of this research is to design and implement a smart network gateway using REST API to enhance the efficiency and security of data transmission in the aquaculture sector. The increasing need for aquaculture farmers to monitor environmental conditions in real time requires an effective and secure data transmission system. The purpose of the proposed system is to ensure data transmission is more secure and efficient by combining data compression algorithms such as GZIP and ZLIB with AES encryption. This study evaluates the system's performance in real-world scenarios by comparing data size and transmission duration with and without compression and encryption. The study's findings indicate that ZLIB is more efficient in compressing data compared to GZIP, and that combining ZLIB with AES results in the most efficient data size and transmission duration. The system's ability to integrate with IoT infrastructure enables real-time monitoring, improving productivity and operational efficiency in aquaculture.

Author Keywords: representational state transfer application platform interface

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Early Warning System for Transformer Faults at 20KV Distribution Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an internet of things (IoT)-based early warning system for transformer disturbances at a 20KV distribution substation. This system is designed for real-time monitoring of distribution substations over long distances. system is designed as a solution to problems that often occur in 20KV distribution substations where the transformers show different usage patterns at peak load times. This occurs when usage is high during the day and low at night. This research is a solution to provide protection for distribution substations against conditions that have the potential to cause damage or system failure to transformer components. Distribution transformers are one of the vital components of the electric power system infrastructure. The heat produced by electromagnetic energy can increase the temperature of the transformer and potentially damage the components inside, so temperature is the main thing whose value must be measured and monitored at all times to ensure that the components in the substation remain safe. Temperature can be sensed using the DS18B20 sensor, and the reading results of the environment can be accessed remotely using IoT media. From the test results of this system, it was found that the load ratio calculation on the transformer during the day was around 516.67 kVA, equivalent to 41.336% of the load, while at night it was around 414.65 kVA, equivalent to 33.172% of the load. A transformer with a capacity of 1250 kVA may be loaded continuously when the temperature is around 20°C, whereas under installation conditions at a temperature of around 30°C, it can only be loaded 90%.

articleTitle: Smart Farming Design with NodeMCU ESP32 for NFT HYDROPONIC
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Hydroponic farming is a creative solution to the problem of using limited natural resources and limited land. In this regard, this research aims to develop and implement a smart farming system for hydroponics. The system uses software, microcontroller, and sensor technology to monitor plants, improve resource use efficiency, and control environmental parameters of plant growth. The system is equipped with sensors and actuators connected through NodeMCU ESP32 to monitor and control plant conditions in real-time. This system can increase efficiency and transparency in the agricultural industry, as well as improve the quality and profit of farmers. The smart farming system can monitor nutrients, pH and temperature in hydroponic plants in real-time. In addition, the system also allows for web-based remotely accessible control and independent decision-making by the microcontroller.

articleTitle: Car Detection Using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) Features on Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles are becoming a significant innovation trend in the global automotive industry along with the development of automotive technology. This autonomous vehicle concept promises revolutionary possibilities in transportation in the future. In autonomous vehicles, car detection is very necessary to support the car navigation system using the computer vision method. This research aims to propose car detection using a Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and a Vector Support Machine (SVM). The HOG feature extraction will extract the car image objects, thereby enabling autonomous vehicle systems to identify cars with high accuracy. On the other hand, the SVM classifier is used for the car detection process and separates car objects from other objects besides cars from the HOG features. The detection result showed that car detection accuracy was 83%. This indicates that the car detection in this research is successful and can be implemented on autonomous vehicle navigation systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Function Control Device Apps
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The development of technology is one thing that humans cannot avoid, especially from the use of gadgets used by parents, adults, and especially children. The role of parents is very much needed in the family to accompany and supervise children's use of gadgets. The aim of this research is to facilitate parental supervision of children remotely. The method used in developing this system is the Extreme Programming method, which is an Agile Software Development Methodologies development methodology. The results of this research are Multi-Function Control Device Apps, with the name “Kids Monitoring.” Multi-Function Control Device Apps is an application that can help parents monitor their children when using gadgets. Based on the results of the questionnaire, 80% of respondents agreed that they had difficulty monitoring children's gadget use, so this application is one solution to monitor children from excessive gadget use. According to 75% of respondents, the features in the Kids Monitoring application can be easily understood. 96% of respondents felt that the features in the Kids Monitoring application were quite complete and useful so that parents felt helped in managing their child's gadget use. This research can be further developed with artificial intelligence technology because technology is increasingly sophisticated and continues to develop, so that it can create new features related to artificial intelligence itself

articleTitle: Modernizing the Hairstyle Selection Experience Based on Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Barbershop is an advancement or development in the fashion industry for determining desired hairstyles according to facial shapes. This research explores the implementation of augmented reality (AR) technology in barbershops as a solution to modernize the hair style selection experience. Using the Scrum method, this research focuses on facilitating customers in choosing a hairstyle that suits their facial shape. The system not only enhances barbershop efficiency but also provides a unique and engaging experience for customers, opening up innovation potential in the web-based barbershop world. Questionnaire results indicate that 70% of respondents are satisfied and comfortable with the augmented reality-based modernization application for hair style selection experience, and 50% recommend this application for general public use. Overall, 65% of respondents feel satisfied with the quality of the augmented reality-based modernization application for hair style selection experience. To enhance the feasibility of recommendations, future research is expected to develop by adding a 360-degree feature to detect all sides of the head.

articleTitle: Identifying of Student Succes Based on Grades of State Madrasah Aliyah Students in Bandung City Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research aims to identify the values of madrasa students in Bandung City using machine learning techniques. The application of technology in the education sector, primarily through machine learning, can provide significant benefits in analyzing complex and large amounts of academic data. In this study, several machine learning algorithms are applied to analysis student grade data from various subjects and data that influence student success in getting good grades. The analysis results show that the Naïve Bayes algorithm is the most effective in predicting and classifying based on student grades and other supporting data, with an accuracy of 98.5%. Compared with other algorithms used in this research, the results were Random Forest 98.4%, Decision Tree 95.3% and Logistic Regression 71.9%. These findings indicate that using machine learning in the academic assessment process in madrasas increases efficiency and provides deeper insights for better decision-making in the field of education.

articleTitle: Vehicle Path Tracking Using Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research focuses on the development and implementation of a vehicle motion capture system using the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) as the sole source of inertial data, with the ESP32 as the main controlling microcontroller. The IMU is used to measure the linear acceleration and angular velocity of the vehicle in three dimensions, which are then processed to estimate the vehicle's position and orientation. The ESP32 was chosen because of its powerful capabilities in data processing, low power consumption, and wireless connectivity that allows real-time data transmission. The system aims to provide an efficient and cost-effective solution for motion capture applications, especially in environments where GPS technology is unreliable, such as inside tunnels or tall buildings. By processing data using filter algorithms, this system tries to reduce cumulative errors such as drift, which generally occur in IMU sensors. Initial test results show that the system can achieve a sufficient level of accuracy for basic navigation and vehicle movement monitoring applications. This abstract explores the potential and limitations of IMU and ESP32-based motion capture approaches and discusses the implications and possibilities for further developments in autonomous vehicle technology and navigation systems.

articleTitle: Applying Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for Data Base District Road Pavement Condition: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the database of district road pavement conditions offers a robust and efficient method for monitoring and managing infrastructure. This study aims to model and analyze the condition of road pavements using GIS, incorporating various parameters such as damage type, severity, and location. By integrating spatial data and attribute information, the GIS platform facilitates comprehensive visualization and interpretation of pavement conditions. Validation of the system shows a high accuracy rate of 95%, with data verified from reliable sources. The GIS model significantly enhances decision-making processes, providing stakeholders with a clear and accessible tool for infrastructure management. The results demonstrate that GIS is an effective solution for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of road maintenance and rehabilitation strategies.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Commercial 2.45GHz Wireless Power Transmission System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: A Microwave-Based Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) system was developed to enhance UAVs' operational capabilities during emergencies. It includes an RF power generator and an integrated antenna design combining RLSA and conical horn elements. Measurements showed optimal antenna parameters: S11-32.669, VSWR near 1.098, and 17.32 dB gain. The system achieved an output power of 510.505Watts from the RF generator and 4197.5898 dB with the integrated antenna. The system can transmit up to 11.5dBmAdditionally, it safely transmitted power at 0.0645 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> around the antenna, below the 5 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> human exposure limit.

articleTitle: Leveraging Heart Rate Variability and Machine Learning for Daily Activity Classification in Healthy Adult Males
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Advancements in machine learning techniques for analyzing heart rate variability (HRV) show great potential in accurately measuring various activities in the field of health monitoring. This work examines the feasibility of using non-invasive HRV data gathered during everyday activities to train machine learning models for accurate activity classification. In the field of personalization, the study focuses on the difficulty of adapting to individual differences in baseline HRV. It also acknowledges that HRV is influenced by stress, physical activity, and external influences, and that it is a dynamic measure. The experimental methodology consists of a pilot study using a retrospective observational cohort approach. It utilizes a waistband device to continuously record heart rate variability (HRV) during different daily activities. The study utilizes a thorough methodology that includes statistical data description, correlation analysis, variance analysis, outlier detection, and identification of cycle periods using power spectral density. The performance of various machine learning models, such as Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression, was evaluated for activity classification. The Decision Tree model exhibited superior performance. The work provides useful insights into the potential of machine learning for HRV-based activity monitoring, highlighting the importance of collecting reliable data and developing tailored models to improve accuracy and practicality.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Real-Time Safety Vest and Helmet Detection Using Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Workplace safety is a critical priority in the industry, particularly in enforcing occupational health and safety (OHS) standards. This study introduces an innovative OHS compliance inspection system integrating access control with object recognition technology. The system captures images of workers using an ESP32Cam as the pre-processing step for safety helmet and vest detection. The ESP32 Cam captures the best image for detection at a maximum distance of 100 cm. The OpenCV library accesses these images, while the YOLOv8 library performs object recognition. The dataset includes 761 images for helmets and 314 images for vests, with the best results achieved using 100 training epochs of the pre-trained yolov8s.pt model. The system demonstrates a confidence level of 0.89 and an accuracy rate 0.75 in identifying safety helmets and vests. Recognition results are monitored in real-time via a web-based dashboard, with data stored in a database for further analysis. This study highlights the potential of integrating object recognition technology to enhance OHS compliance and workplace safety.

articleTitle: Evaluating Time Series Approaches for Cellular Network Traffic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This paper examines the predictive accuracy of four distinct models-ARIMA, ARMA, AR, and Linear Regression-applied to network traffic forecasting. Through a comprehensive analysis, the ARIMA model was identified as the most effective for non-stationary data, demonstrating its robustness in capturing complex temporal patterns. The linear regression model, however, outperformed the others across the dataset, with the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 1.223 and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.106, indicating minimal prediction errors. The results underscore the importance of selecting appropriate models based on data characteristics and prediction requirements. Furthermore, the study highlights the potential of linear regression, a relatively simple method, to outperform more complex time series models under specific conditions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Upselling Model in Customer Relationship Management for Revenue Maximization in Telecommunications Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: In this rapid era of business and commerce, it is crucial to build long-term customer relationships to maximize a company's revenue. To increase the growth and profitability of the telecommunications industry, up-selling strategies can be employed. In our research, we explore the use of predictive modeling and recommendation systems in Customer Relationship Management (CRM), with a specific focus on up-selling techniques. Utilizing a wide-ranging data set that includes various customer attributes, we employed six supervised machine learning techniques to create predictive models for the telecommunications industry around the world, namely XGBoost, HistGradientBoost, random forest, naive bayes, k-nearest neighbor and decision tree. We evaluated the performance of each model to reveal which algorithm performs best. We found that XGBoost turns out to be the most applicable and reliable model for upsell applications, with an accuracy of 0.96.

articleTitle: A Wireless Sensor Network Integrated with Edge Computing for Real-Time Crop Monitoring and Automated Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Cloud-based smart agriculture systems struggle with real-time processing and connectivity in remote areas. This study integrates edge computing with WSNs to create a real-time crop monitoring and auto-irrigation system. The edge node handles RF communication with sensor and actuator nodes and connects to a LoRaWAN gateway provided by Packetworx using an SX1276 LoRa chip at 868 MHz. This design allows efficient data collection, local processing, and automated control without needing constant internet access. Implemented in Rosario, Batangas, Philippines, the system monitors soil moisture, NPK levels, temperature, and humidity, and controls irrigation via five solenoid valves. Each node operates for about 10.3 hours, extended by solar panels. Connectivity tests indicate better signal quality with higher gateways and increased packet loss at greater distances.

articleTitle: Enhance Low-Resolution Face Recognition Accuracy Using Median and Mean Filtering Techniques Based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of median and mean filtering techniques in enhancing the performance of deep learning-based face recognition systems on low-resolution images. The main challenge in face recognition lies in the low quality of images due to various factors such as lighting, distance, and camera resolution. Median filtering replaces each pixel with the median value of its neighbors, effectively removing salt-and-pepper noise, while mean filtering replaces each pixel with the average value of its neighbors, resulting in smoother images but potentially blurring important details. The results show that median filtering is more effective in preserving edge details and reducing speckle noise, whereas mean filtering excels at producing overall smoother images. The combination of these techniques is expected to enhance the accuracy of face recognition on low-resolution images, contributing to the development of more reliable and precise face recognition systems

articleTitle: LiDAR: Digitalization of Urban Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This study employed bibliometric analysis to investigate the evolution of LiDAR (Light detection and ranging) as an urban infrastructure monitoring tool over the past decade. Using research articles sourced from Dimensions app, the study aims to identify trends in LiDAR utilization, publication rates, research areas, prolific researchers, geographic distribution, and potential future research directions. The results of the study show that there were 76,861 articles published during the period 2014–2024. The year 2023 was the most productive year. Meanwhile, based on VOSviewer app, LiDAR's versatility has enabled its use in various areas, including building inspection, transportation infrastructure, and traffic analysis. Engineering is the major research area using LiDAR, with 22,256 articles. Albert Ansmann, a scientist from German, is the most prolific researcher over the past decade, having published 100 research articles in the field of LiDAR.

articleTitle: Utilization of Machine Learning Regression Models for Predicting Coverage in Celular Network
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of telecommunication technology, particularly the rollout of 5G networks, predicting signal coverage accurately has become essential for optimizing base station placement and assessing network efficiency. This study aims to develop and evaluate machine learning regression models to predict signal coverage in both urban and suburban areas. We explore several regression algorithms, including Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Lasso Regression, Decision Tree Regression, Random Forest Regression, Gradient Boosting Regression, Support Vector Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors Regression, and XGBoost Regression. Data for this study were collected through drive tests using G-Net Track Pro and cellular operator data, which included parameters such as signal strength, transmitter and receiver heights, the distance between transmitter and receiver, frequency, altitude, elevation angle, tilting offset angle, and horizontal and vertical distances from the boresight. The performance of these models was assessed using metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2})$</tex>. Among the tested models, Random Forest Regression demonstrated the highest accuracy, with an MSE of 9.56, MAE of 2.08, RMSE of 3.09, and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> of 0.85. These results highlight the potential of Random Forest Regression as a reliable tool for predicting 5G signal coverage in various environments.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Prevention Methods of Virtual Machine Environment Recognition by Malware
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Virtual Machine (VM) environment recognition or Anti-virtual machine (anti-VM) is one of the strategies employed by malware to evade detection. Virtual machines are frequently used for dynamic malware analysis. Using anti-VM techniques, malware can detect the presence of a VM and alter its behavior accordingly. To address this challenge, an effective approach involves first identifying the specific anti-VM techniques used by the malware, and then building protection within the VM to prevent malware from obscuring its actions. Anti-Vmtechniques typically search for indicators of a virtualized environment. These parameters include specific parameters such as the filesystem structure, running processes, and Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). When malware detects these parameters, it may hide its functionality to evade detection. In this paper, we present a study on anti-VM techniques and describe the development of a tool designed to resist the anti-VM techniques on VirtualBox. This tool was implemented using PowerShell scripts and compiled into an executable (.exe) file. We tested the tool with well-known anti-VM detection programs, SEMS and Pafish. The results demonstrate that this tool can successfully mask several VM artifact parameters and prevent malware from recognizing the virtual environment.

articleTitle: Development of Mapoint Learning Media in Grade 12 Statistics
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The background of this research is based on the emergence of students' difficulties in understanding statistical material, and the lack of development of learning media related such material. The purpose of this research is to develop MAPOINT learning media on statistics material. This research utilizes Research and Development (R&D) research and development procedures by adapting the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation) model. The research took place at Senior High School no. 1 South Tangerang with 29 grade 12 students consisting of a small class of 4 and a large class of 25 and 1 math teacher as test subjects. The validation results of MAPOINT learning media on media aspects were 80.82%, material aspects are 96.67%, language aspects are 96.18% which means they are very valid. The results of the MAPOINT learning media trial in small classes showed a positive response from 4 subjects. The results of the MAPOINT learning media trial in large classes of 25 students obtained an average of 85.56% with very practical criteria, while one Mathematics teacher obtained an average of 98.08% with very practical criteria. The results of this study are expected to be useful for teachers, students, and researchers.

articleTitle: Analysis on Performance of Semi-Real-Time Transcription on Health App
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The fragmentation of health information systems has hindered seamless data exchange in healthcare services, posing challenges in achieving efficient, real-time access to patient health data. This study addresses these issues by evaluating the implementation of a semi-real-time transcription system using a distributed architecture with a message broker to enhance the documentation of clinical examination processes in primary health services. The research focuses on assessing the feasibility of this approach by measuring key performance indicators such as latency and word error rate (WER) during clinical conversation transcription. Audio recordings were segmented into shorter fragments to simulate real-time transcription, and data transmission was conducted through the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP). The findings demonstrate that the average latencys achieved by semi-real-time transcription system is 7.7s, indicating its potential suitability for clinical documentation applications that do not require strict real-time processing. However, glitches observed in the message broker's forwarding mechanism suggest the need for further optimization to ensure consistent performance. Future work aims to develop strategies to minimize transcription errors, enhance reliability, and improve the overall integration of this system in healthcare settings. This study contributes to the advancement of health information systems by offering architecture into scalable and effective methods for semi-real-time data transcription and interoperability.

articleTitle: Implementation of Transmit Power Adaptation Algorithm on VANET Testbed Using SDN OpenFlow
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: In vehicular networks (VANETs), periodic beaconing is crucial for guaranteeing vehicle safety and improving traffic efficiency. However, frequent beaconing with high transmission power can lead to co-channel interference and reduce beacon reception ratio. This paper proposes an implementation of a Transmit Power Adaptation (TPA) algorithm on a VANET testbed using the OpenFlow protocol. The TPA algorithm dynamically adjusts the transmission power of vehicles based on network conditions to achieve a balance between communication range and beacon reception ratio. The OpenFlow protocol is employed to enable centralized control and efficient resource management within the VANET testbed. The paper details the system model, the TPA algorithm design, and the implementation using the OpenFlow protocol. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces co-channel interference and improves beacon reception ratio compared to fixed transmission power schemes.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Smart Smile: Early Detection of Mental Health Conditions Through Computational Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The early detection of mental health conditions is crucial for timely intervention and effective treatment. This study presents the development and evaluation of the “Smart Smile” application, an AI-powered tool designed to detect early signs of mental health issues using computational intelligence. The primary objective of this research is to design a robust system that leverages artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to analyze user interactions and biometric data to identify potential mental health concerns. The scope of the study includes the integration of various data sources such as facial expressions, voice tone, text input, and user behavior patterns. The methods employed in this research encompass data collection through user surveys and real-time monitoring, followed by the application of machine learning techniques for data analysis. Specifically, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and natural language processing (NLP) algorithms are utilized to process and interpret the collected data. Key findings from this study indicate that the Smart Smile application can accurately predict early signs of conditions such as depression and anxiety with a high degree of accuracy. The application's performance is validated through extensive testing and cross-validation against established mental health assessment tools. The results demonstrate the potential of AI and computational intelligence in enhancing mental health diagnostics and providing users with actionable insights. In conclusion, the AI-powered Smart Smile application represents a significant advancement in the field of mental health care, offering a scalable and accessible solution for early detection of mental health conditions. Future work will focus on improving the algorithm's accuracy, expanding the dataset, and integrating additional features to support a broader range of mental health conditions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Naïve Bayes and Random Forest on Sentiment Analysis of Brand Reputation Provider Live. On
publicationTitle: 2024 18th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Internet users in Indonesia continue to increase yearly, reaching 215.63 million people in 2022. However, many internet users in Indonesia complain about the services provided by internet service providers. This complaint arises because the service provider does not provide full control over the use of data services and the distribution of quotas that are not appropriate. To solve this problem, Live. On is here as a new digital service provider to improve the user experience. To evaluate the success of Live. On, a sentiment analysis was carried out through the Google Play platform to see user feedback regarding the services provided. In this study, data was collected through a data scraping process on Google Play. Furthermore, the data were analyzed using the Naïve Bayes and Random Forest classification methods. The Net Reputation Score (NRS) calculation is used to measure the level of user satisfaction. The comparison results show that when the SMOTE technique is not used, Random Forest performs better than Naïve Bayes. Random Forest has 80.37% accuracy, 61% precision, 58% recall, and 57% f1-score, while Naïve Bayes has 80% accuracy, 54% precision, 58% recall, and 56% f1-score. When the SMOTE technique is applied, Random Forest still performs better with 78% accuracy, 79% precision, 78% recall, and 78% f1-score, while Naïve Bayes has the same performance on all metrics with 73%. In addition, based on NRS calculations using Naïve Bayes prediction results, Live. On provider reputation has a value of −33.08%, while using Random Forest prediction results, its reputation reaches −41.08%. Both reputation scores are below average, so Live. On is considered to have a poor reputation. Therefore, Live. On needs to fix complaints felt by users to improve its reputation.
